ai-at-work.title: AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
ai-at-work.excerpt: On Equity, we discuss why tech CEO statements can seem so tone deaf.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Tech CEOs are publicly championing AI as a productivity miracle while their own workforces deal with layoffs, retraining chaos, and genuine uncertainty about what their jobs will look like next year. This matters because digital workplace leaders are caught in the middle, tasked with managing both the AI rollout and the real anxiety it's creating on the ground. The truth is, if your biggest concern is how AI makes executive life easier while your employees are wondering if they'll be here in six months, you're not building a digital workplace strategy, you're building a morale disaster.

ai-at-work.title: Marble Cognition raises $3.75M for its AI agent workers that watch and learn how people work
ai-at-work.excerpt: Artificial intelligence agents have become two a penny in the enterprise today, but just because they’re rapidly being commoditized does not mean organizations know how best to use them. That’s the ch
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Marble Cognition just raised 3.75 million dollars to build AI agents that watch how people actually work and learn from their behavior patterns. This matters because most organizations are drowning in AI tools they don't know how to deploy effectively, so anything that bridges the gap between AI capabilities and real workflow adoption is worth paying attention to. The irony is thick though: we're funding AI to watch us work so we can deploy more AI to do our work, when maybe the real problem is we never asked people what they actually need in the first place.

ai-at-work.title: Project-by-project security reviews can’t keep pace with enterprise AI agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: Enterprises racing to put AI agents into production are finding that tokenization and other data protection methods now decide how fast those projects move. But sensitive data fed into models is hard
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are shipping AI agents faster than their security teams can review them, and once sensitive data gets fed into these models it's basically permanent. This matters because digital workplace leaders are now caught between business pressure to deploy AI and the reality that their security processes were built for a different speed. Here's the thing: you can't unring a bell, and feeding your company's confidential stuff into an AI model without proper governance is like giving your keys to someone and hoping they won't lose them.

ai-at-work.title: Agent demand can’t be forecast, meaning the database has to be ready for anything
ai-at-work.excerpt: Enterprises building an agentic AI architecture are learning that the database matters as much as the model. AI agents fire off thousands of unplanned queries at once — and expect answers in milliseco
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Enterprises are discovering that AI agents generate unpredictable, massive database query loads that demand millisecond response times, pushing database technology to its limits. For digital workplace pros, this means your infrastructure decisions around AI deployment can't be guesswork anymore because agents will absolutely expose weak database architecture under real-world conditions. The irony is rich: we spent decades optimizing for predictable user behavior, and now machines are going to make our databases work harder than humans ever did.

digital-culture.title: The hidden cost of workplace transformation: How change initiatives crush top employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Nearly half of employees report experiencing "transformation fatigue," according to a recent study
digital-culture.dwp_take: Microsoft and Slack just conducted research showing that nearly half of all employees are burnt out from constant workplace transformation initiatives. This matters because digital workplace leaders keep launching shiny new tools and processes without accounting for the cognitive load they create, which directly causes your best people to quit. Here's the thing: nobody's ever been retained by change for change's sake, and transformation fatigue is just a fancy way of saying we've finally admitted that rolling out Slack, Teams, a new intranet, and agile workflows in the same quarter was a terrible idea.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are finally waking up to the fact that you can't build decent AI without clean workforce data, and people managers are making this a top priority for 2025. This matters because for years we've watched organizations slap AI onto broken processes and call it innovation, so getting the data foundation right actually prevents expensive disasters down the road. The funny part is that "workforce data as a priority" has been obvious since about 2015, so we're basically celebrating organizations for catching up to what they should have done a decade ago.

industry-news.title: Before You Buy a Second Monitor, See if Your Tablet Can Do the Job
industry-news.excerpt: Your tablet could double as a second monitor. Here's how Samsung Second Screen and Apple Sidecar work, and when a dedicated display is worth buying. The post Before You Buy a Second Monitor, See if Yo
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic ran through how tablets like iPads and Samsung devices can function as secondary monitors through native OS features like Apple Sidecar and Samsung Second Screen. This matters because it challenges the assumption that everyone needs to drop money on a dedicated external display, and it's a real option for people working from home or in hybrid setups. That said, after thirty years watching workarounds get mistaken for solutions, I'll tell you that a proper monitor is still worth the investment if you're doing this work eight hours a day, because your eyes and neck will thank you later.

industry-news.title: Singapore’s Swap Mobile Lets You Change Phones Every Six Months — Here’s How It Works
industry-news.excerpt: Singapore’s Swap Mobile offers phone upgrades every six months, with flexible handset options and a new 24-month contract for each eligible switch. The post Singapore’s Swap Mobile Lets You Change Pho
industry-news.dwp_take: Singapore just launched Swap Mobile, which lets people upgrade their phones every six months instead of waiting two years like the rest of us suckers. This matters to digital workplace leaders because device management just got messier, from tracking mobile fleet lifecycles to managing security patches across constantly rotating hardware. Honestly, I give it six months before IT departments start asking why employees need a new phone more often than they need a performance review.

industry-news.title: Replacing workers with AI? You may come to regret it
industry-news.excerpt: New research from Gartner suggests that poor workforce planning means many companies will up rehiring staff
industry-news.dwp_take: Gartner's research shows companies that rushed to cut headcount and replace workers with AI are now scrambling to rehire because they didn't think through their actual operational needs. This matters because it proves what we've known for decades: technology is a tool that amplifies your strategy, not a substitute for having one. Here's the real kicker though - the companies that nail this aren't the ones picking between humans or AI, they're the ones figuring out what work actually needs doing first, then deciding who or what does it best.

industry-news.title: Lakeside Software taps Mark Benson to lead EMEA channel strategy
industry-news.excerpt: The appointment comes as the digital employee experience (DEX) vendor looks to expand its partner ecosystem around the SysTrack platform
industry-news.dwp_take: Lakeside Software hired Mark Benson to head up their European, Middle Eastern, and African channel operations as they push to grow their partner network around SysTrack. This matters because how vendors distribute and support their tools through partners directly affects which DEX platforms actually get implemented and used in real organizations, not just demoed to willing audiences. Benson's got big shoes to fill in a market where everyone's suddenly an expert in employee experience, which is a polite way of saying the channel game in DEX is getting crowded and competitive as hell.
